meta.name: Training Sanctum — Flashcards UX Design DNA
meta.description: Synthesized design identity for Training Sanctum's flashcard/spaced-repetition app: color palette and editorial grid rhythm drawn from the official Spy x Family anime portal (spy-family.net), app structure and component shapes drawn from Quizlet's library and flashcard-study surfaces, reconciled against PRD non-goals (no gamification, no illustration, dark-mode default).
source_references: spy-family.net official anime portal (screenshot) — color palette + editorial grid layout
Quizlet library/folder view (screenshot) — sidebar nav, list-row structure
Quizlet flashcard/study view (screenshot) — review card shape, progress counter, control row

secondary.role: light-mode default background (sage/olive green, measured from spy-family.net)

accent.role: single pop accent across both modes — primary actions, 'Again' danger grade, section-marker bullets

neutral.usage: Lightest two (#faf7f0 off-white, #ecf1f2 near-white) are text/card-surface colors in dark mode and card-surface in light mode; mid tones are borders/secondary text/disabled states; darkest three (#262838 card, #1a1b24 elevated, #0e0e12 text-on-light/ink) anchor dark-mode surfaces and light-mode text.

color.contrast_strategy: Dual-theme, dark-mode default per PRD §7. DARK (default): background #14151f, card #1f2130, elevated #262838, text #ecf1f2/#faf7f0 — sage is intentionally near-absent (appears only as a muted border/structure tint, not a visible fill). LIGHT (toggle): background #8ea89b (sage, measured from spy-family.net), card #faf7f0 (white, measured), text #0e0e12 (charcoal/ink, measured). The accent #b74242 (measured red) is identical in both modes and is the only saturated color either theme relies on — semantic success/warning/info are desaturated so the accent stays singular.

typography.font_style_notes: System sans-serif throughout, no custom webfonts (locked decision). Headers lean bold/black-weight to echo spy-family.net's masthead confidence; body stays regular-weight for readability during long review sessions. Mono reserved for numeric displays (progress counter 'X / Y', streak count, stats figures).

spacing.section_rhythm: Generous gaps (32–48px) between major page sections and around the review card; tighter, list-like rhythm (8–12px) within folder/card-management rows, matching Quizlet's library density.

layout.grid_system: 12-column responsive grid for folder/stats/import screens; single-column, centered focal layout for the review session
layout.max_content_width: 1200px for app shell content; review card constrained to ~640px centered
layout.columns: Sidebar (fixed ~240px) + fluid content area on desktop; single column with bottom/collapsed nav on mobile
layout.alignment_tendency: strict grid for list/grid views (folders, stats, import mapping table); centered for the review session's focal card

shape.border_usage: subtle 1px borders on inputs and card edges; most separation comes from surface-color contrast rather than borders (dark mode) or shadow (light mode)
shape.divider_style: thin 1px hairline, low-contrast, used sparingly between list rows and under section headers

elevation.depth_cues: shadows plus surface-color layering — card surfaces are a lighter step than the page background rather than relying on heavy shadow

motion.easing: ease-out for entrances, ease-in-out for state transitions
motion.philosophy: minimal functional — motion exists only to clarify a state change (card reveal, grade feedback, row removal), never decorative. Review-loop transitions must stay under the PRD's sub-100ms perceived-latency NFR (FR-9).

components.button_style: soft-rounded filled primary button in accent red; ghost/outline secondary buttons; small tag-style chips use full pill radius, but primary/secondary buttons use medium radius (less pill-extreme than Quizlet's fully rounded buttons)
components.input_style: rounded rectangle inputs, subtle 1px border, accent-colored focus ring
components.card_style: large soft-rounded surface for the review card (elevated above background, center-aligned content, same bounds before/after reveal per locked decision); smaller rounded tiles for folder/library browsing
components.navigation_pattern: left icon+label sidebar (Quizlet-derived structure), five flat sections: Review, Folders, Import, Stats, Settings
components.modal_style: centered rounded modal with scrim overlay, used sparingly (e.g. folder-delete confirmation, restore-from-backup confirmation)
components.list_style: rows grouped under section headers (Quizlet's date-grouping pattern, repurposed for folder/alphabetical grouping), hover-highlight state, trailing '...' overflow menu, small red square bullet as the section-header marker (spy-family.net motif)
components.component_notes: Grade buttons (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are flat/outline style, deliberately non-gamified — no badges, confetti, or mascot imagery; the accent red is reserved for the primary action and the 'Again' state, not spread evenly across all four grades, so the UI doesn't imply false symmetry between the grades (PRD FR-8 binding note).

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: a well-kept study journal / field notebook crossed with a focused reading app
aesthetic.era_influence: contemporary developer-tool minimalism (2020s) with a single editorial-print accent
aesthetic.genre: utilitarian productivity tool with editorial-accent branding

visual_language.ornamentation: subtle accents only (small red square bullets, thin dividers) — no decorative patterns or illustration
visual_language.whitespace_usage: generous around the review card and primary actions; tighter, denser list rows for browsing/management screens
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: a single focal element dominates each screen — the card in review, the list in browsing — chrome recedes around it
visual_language.contrast_level: moderate-to-high for text legibility; color contrast is concentrated in the one accent rather than spread across the UI

composition.hierarchy_method: spatial isolation plus color weight — the accent red marks the one actionable thing per screen
composition.balance_type: symmetric and centered in the review session; asymmetric sidebar+content split in browsing screens
composition.flow_direction: top-to-bottom, center-weighted in review; left-sidebar-to-content in browsing
composition.grouping_strategy: date-style or alphabetical section headers grouping list rows, consistent with Quizlet's library pattern
composition.negative_space_role: active — negative space is what signals 'focus mode' (FR-11): chrome is removed entirely during review, not merely minimized

imagery.illustration_style: none — no character art or illustration; this is a utilitarian app, not the promotional portal it draws color from
imagery.graphic_elements: small red square bullet accents (lifted from spy-family.net) used only as section markers
imagery.image_shape: n/a — no imagery used in the product UI

interaction_feel.feedback_style: immediate and understated — color/opacity shift on hover or state change, no bounce or elastic motion
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: row/card background lightens one step on hover; no scale transforms
interaction_feel.transition_personality: snappy (sub-100ms perceived) in the review loop; smooth fade elsewhere
interaction_feel.loading_style: skeleton or subtle fade-in, no personality-driven spinners
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: low — motion is reserved for state changes that matter (reveal, grade, row delete), not used decoratively

brand_voice_in_ui.formality: casual-professional, like a well-made developer tool
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: calm and informative — e.g. the empty due-queue state shows streak + a quick-add shortcut, not an apology or decoration
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: plain, specific, non-alarming — inline field errors, per-line import error reporting with line number + reason

overview.fallback_strategy: n/a — no effects layer exists to disable; CSS-only throughout, by deliberate constraint (PRD non-goals rule out visual flourish)

background_effects.description: Flat solid-color surfaces only; no gradients, noise, or animated backgrounds.

3d_elements.description: Not used — no 3D/WebGL surface anywhere in this product.

text_effects.description: Static text only; no split-letter, typewriter, glitch, or gradient-fill effects.

image_effects.description: No imagery in the product UI, so no image effects apply.

canvas_drawings.description: Not used as a visual effect. Note: FR-15's interval-distribution bar chart is a standard data-visualization component (SVG or charting-library bar chart), not a 'visual effect' in this dimension's sense — it carries no bespoke rendering beyond a normal chart.

visual_effects.composite_notes: This product deliberately carries no visual-effects layer — the PRD rules out gamification and decorative flourish, and the brief's portfolio goal is algorithmic/testing rigor, not visual spectacle. The two source references diverge sharply in this dimension (spy-family.net is an image-heavy promotional portal; Quizlet's own site also uses none of these effects in the screens referenced), but neither contributes anything here since Training Sanctum only borrows their color/structure, not their media richness. Measured palettes above come from scripts/measure-colors.mjs run against the three reference screenshots (spy-family.net portal, Quizlet library view, Quizlet flashcard-study view).
